name: W23 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)
description:
Fifteen minutes, three parts: primer, work, then the deep stretch arc. Work before stretches — warm muscle stretches further.

This week rotates roughly half the moves again. The hip-flexor lunge and inchworm return to the front, plank shoulder-taps join the work block, and two W12-era favorites — couch stretch and frog stretch — come back into the yoga arc. The rehab cluster and the pushup greasing set never rotate.

exercises.notes: Full range both directions, breathing with the movement. Slow — the spine's first move of the day.
**Back in the rotation.** 45s each side. Half-kneeling, tuck the pelvis and sink forward — feel the front of the back hip. Counters all the sitting; primes the hips before anything.
Standing, hinged slightly forward. Tight fists, thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension.
**Greasing set — never to failure.** Leave 2-3 in the tank. Elbows ~45°, **pack down not up**. A daily habit, not a training set.
**New this week.** From a plank, tap the opposite shoulder without letting the hips rock. **Hips DEAD STILL** — the anti-rotation is the whole point; if they sway, slow down or widen the feet.
**Ribs DOWN, low back flat to the floor.** That contact is the exercise — if the back arches off the floor, shorten the reach.
**Back in the rotation.** From standing, hinge and walk the hands out to a plank, hold a beat, walk back. Hamstrings on the way out, full-body brace at the plank.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Deep Stretch Arc (~7 min)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Thoracic + hip flexor opener. Top leg crosses, chest stays down.
**Back in the rotation.** 30s each side. From down dog, drive the knee toward the same-side elbow/head, then reach it back to the sky. Core + hip mobility in one flowing move.
45s each side. Deep hip opener. Forearms down if the hip allows, hands if not.
Bodyweight, slow. Sit into one hip, other leg straight, heel down. **Take note of how these feel** — an early read on how fresh the legs are before any training.

**Back in the rotation — a W12-era favorite.** 45s each side. Back foot up on a wall/couch, tall torso. Deep hip-flexor and quad stretch — the strong counter to all the squatting and lunging this week.
**Back in the rotation.** Knees wide, sink the hips back. Adductors — the figure-8 and Cossack work bill here.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **PUSH DAY.** 45s each arm at MID elbow height.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Face down, arms in a Y, lift with the lower traps. Slow, small range.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Plank, arms locked, only the blades move.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Elbow pinned to the ribs, small controlled range. Light or no weight.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Back flat to the wall, arms slide keeping contact. Where it leaves the wall is your real range.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Passive hang, shoulders relaxed.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** From a dead hang, pull the shoulders down without bending the arms.
**LEGS DAY / QL.** 30s each side. QL's been busy — give it the full time.
**LEGS + KB DAY.** 45s each side.
**ANY DAY.** 30s each side.

sets.notes: The six rehab anchors run every day. Add the day-specific pieces on top based on what you're training.

tips: **Order matters: work before stretches.** Warm muscle stretches deeper.
**Rotated in this week:** hip-flexor lunge, plank shoulder-taps, inchworm walkout, down-dog-knee-to-head, couch stretch, frog stretch.
**Rotated out this week:** thread-the-needle, spiderman plank, glute bridge, puppy pose, happy baby, straddle reaches.
**Never rotates:** the six rehab anchors (prone Y, scapular push-up, side-lying ER, wall angel, dead hang, scapular pull) and the pushup greasing set.
**Push-ups leave 2-3 in reserve** — a greasing habit, never a training set.
**Cossacks are an early warning system** — if they feel tired here, the legs are tired before the session starts.
Not too hard, not too long — this precedes training, it doesn't replace it.
